milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The lake is centered at (8, 0, 0) relative to spawn. max_distance=5 ensures the player has walked to the lake edge (lake starts at x=4, so player must be at ~x=3-5 to be within 5 blocks of center at x=8). facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is looking toward the water body, confirming visual identification.

Uses inventory_has because the cooked_rabbit is in a remote chest on the far shore at (13,0,0) — the player must navigate past the lake to retrieve it. While this checks retrieval rather than consumption, retrieving the item from this remote location IS the core navigational challenge. This is the best available rule given the 5 supported types (no has_effect rule exists). Known limitation: checks pickup not eating.

Uses inventory_has because mining oak_leaves with shears (provided to player via /give) drops the oak_leaves block item into inventory. No oak_leaves items exist in the player's starting inventory or in any chest, so having oak_leaves in inventory definitively proves the player mined them from the trees on the far shore (x=14).

Uses position_near_with_facing toward the raised cobblestone platform at (15, 1, 3) where the splash potion chest is located. This is a SEPARATE location from the rabbit chest at (13,0,0), preventing milestone overlap. max_distance=2 and facing_tolerance=45 ensure the player has specifically navigated to this distinct platform and is facing the potion chest, confirming they found and accessed it. Known limitation: checks proximity to potion source, not actual potion use.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a golden_hoe places it in the player's inventory. No golden_hoe exists anywhere in the scene initially (not in any chest or player inventory), so having one definitively proves it was crafted from gold ingots + sticks at the crafting table.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a golden_sword places it in the player's inventory. No golden_sword exists anywhere in the scene initially, so having one definitively proves it was crafted from gold ingots + sticks at the crafting table.

Uses inventory_has for iron_ingot because the scene contains ZERO iron ingots — only raw_iron ore (14 total across two chests). The ONLY way to obtain iron_ingot in this scene is by smelting raw_iron in the blast furnace with coal as fuel. Therefore, having iron_ingot in inventory is definitive, irrefutable proof that the player interacted with the blast furnace (opened GUI, placed raw_iron + coal, waited for smelting, retrieved output). This is the strongest possible milestone — leverages scene design constraints for perfect verification.

Uses inventory_has because crafting iron_boots places them in the player's inventory. No iron_boots exist anywhere in the scene initially, so having them definitively proves they were crafted from smelted iron ingots (4 required) at the crafting table.

Uses BOTH inventory_has AND position_near_with_facing toward the anvil. The damaged iron helmet starts in a chest at (-5, 1, -3) and the anvil is at (-5, 1, -5) — 2 blocks apart. inventory_has confirms the player retrieved the helmet; position_near_with_facing toward the anvil (max_distance=2, facing_tolerance=45) confirms the player was at the anvil facing it, which is required to use the anvil GUI for repair. The dual-rule approach provides significantly stronger verification than inventory_has alone — a player who merely grabs the helmet from the chest without visiting the anvil would fail the proximity check.

scene_description: A compact scene with a lake in the center-east area (x=4-11, z=-3 to 3), oak trees on the far shore (x=14), a smithy workshop to the northwest (x=-8 to -4, z=-2 to -6). Player spawns at origin facing east toward the lake. The far shore has two distinct points of interest: a chest with cooked rabbit at (13,0,0) and a raised cobblestone platform with splash potion chest at (15,1,3). The smithy contains a blast furnace, crafting table, and anvil, with chests holding raw iron ore, gold ingots, coal, and a damaged iron helmet. Player is in Survival mode with 30 XP levels and shears.
task_text: Explore the area: find the lake ahead of you, then navigate to the far shore to eat cooked rabbit from the chest and find the splash potion of swiftness on the raised platform nearby. Mine oak leaves from the trees beyond the lake, then use the oak logs to craft sticks and make a golden hoe and golden sword at the smithy's crafting table. At the smithy, smelt raw iron in the blast furnace using coal as fuel, craft iron boots, and repair the damaged iron helmet on the anvil.
design_notes: FINAL VERSION with all validator fixes applied. Three critical fixes: (1) /gamemode survival @p enables hunger for eating. (2) Splash potion in separate chest on cobblestone platform at [15,1,3], distinct from rabbit chest at [13,0,0]. (3) 30 XP levels for anvil repair. Scene radius ~16 blocks. Raw iron forces blast furnace use. Oak trees past lake forces navigation. Shears enable leaf block drops.
